subject: EU strict serving binding request — Mediclear PHI workflows
messages:
From: Lauren McAdams <lauren@mediclear.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Feb 2028 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: EU-only inference & hard model binding for PHI workflows

Hi Tessa / Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. To reiterate from our security and legal review: for the initial Mediclear pilot we need two things enforced at serving time for any PHI-containing calls:

1) All inference must be served from EU-only capacity (no cross-region routing).
2) No automatic model fallback is allowed — we must force a single vetted model variant for the production route.

Both requirements are non-negotiable for the pilot due to our regulator and audit checklist. We attached a short requirements summary (Mediclear_MVP_requirements.pdf) for context.

Questions:
- Can Redwood attest that requests will never be routed outside EU for the specified route?
- If forced-model selection increases latency/cost, what mitigations do you recommend?
- What is a realistic ETA to lock this in for a pilot starting mid‑March?

We want to move quickly but cannot accept any fallback that could route to non-EU model variants. Please escalate.

—Lauren
Lauren McAdams
Director, Platform Integrations
Mediclear Health

Propose a 30‑minute technical sync with your security lead + our ops/product this week — when are you available?

Date: Mon, 6 Feb 2028 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: Mediclear request — quick internal assessment

Folks — looping to get product/ops eyes on Lauren's request. TL;DR: customer requires EU-only serving + hard model pin (no automatic fallback).

Initial thoughts / risks:
- No-fallback for a production route removes a key reliability lever. If a node goes OOM or a model variant becomes temporarily unavailable, there's a higher likelihood of request failures unless we provision spare capacity.
- Forced model selection fragments KV cache (per-model) which increases cold-start / token-cost.
- Kernel and compilation choices: some quantized variants that reduce cost may not be fully parity-tested for accuracy we validated with Mediclear. If they insist on a specific vetted variant, options narrow to reserved nodes or Private deployment.

Options to propose to the customer:
A) Dedicated EU pool (reserved capacity) + no-fallback policy on the route — medium cost, faster to onboard (~3–4 weeks).
B) Private deployment (VPC) — higher cost, highest isolation, ETA ~6–8 weeks.
C) Hosted with canary hard-bind windowed policy — product would allow temporary hard-bind for pilot with tight monitoring and rollback gates (needs legal sign-off).

Please advise product on whether we can approve a time-bound hard-binding exception with strict monitoring and auto-escalate rules. If yes, I'll propose that to the customer with the expected timeline and minimum capacity numbers.

Karthik
Director, Strategic Sales

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Feb 2028 08:16:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Mediclear request — ops feasibility notes

Quick ops feasibility notes — copying previous context: customer requires EU-only + no fallback.

Feasibility & constraints:
- EU-only routing: straightforward if we run on reserved EU nodes (we can set strict routing policies per-tenant). However, we must ensure routing tables and autoscaler do not allow cross-region overflow — that requires a configuration lock and a manual rollback path.
- No-fallback enforcement: we can implement a route-level policy that refuses to select variant siblings or fall back to compatible models. That is implementable but carries SLA risk.
- Impact: increased error-rate probability under degraded conditions unless we provision ~25–40% headroom on reserved capacity. That is due to KV cache fragmentation and lack of fallback.

Minimum ask from Ops to proceed:
1) Signed capacity commitment for at least 1 month (to reserve dedicated EU instances).
2) Legal acceptance of an agreed SLA deviation clause for this pilot (we should include a known-failure mode and escalation runbook).
3) 4 weeks to prepare deployment, stress-test, and update routing controls (can be compressed to 3 weeks with priority resourcing).

Attaching legal_redline_v3.docx which contains the initial language for the SLA deviation clause and measured acceptance criteria we will ask Legal to accept.

—Markus
Head of Production Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Feb 2028 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Decision & proposed rollout for Mediclear — timeboxed hard-bind exception

Team / Tessa — summarizing and next steps for the Mediclear pilot. After review with Legal and Security, Product will approve a timeboxed hard-bind exception under the following controls: 

Decision summary:
- Approve: route-level EU-only enforcement + explicit no-fallback (hard-bind to their vetted model variant).
- Limit: exception is timeboxed to the pilot window (30 days) and requires the ops controls below.

Required controls & deliverables before go-live:
1) Customer to sign a 1-month dedicated capacity commitment (Ops needs this to reserve nodes).
2) Ops to provision EU reserved pool with +30% headroom and perform a 48‑hour soak test.
3) Product to instrument route with strict monitoring: token-level logging, route-level alarms, and automatic alert to on-call if error rate > 0.5% over a 5m window.
4) Legal to accept SLA deviation language (see Markus' redline).
5) Add JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-1382 for runbook and rollback procedures (priority P1).

Timeline & owner suggestions:
- This week: Tessa to confirm customer willingness to sign 1‑month reserve (owner: Tessa).
- Week 1 (Ops): Provision reserved nodes + basic config (owner: Markus).
- Week 2 (Product/Ops): Stress test, monitoring, security sign-off (owners: Priyom / Markus).
- Go/no-go review after soak test with Mediclear security present.

Karthik — please propose this plan to Lauren. If they accept the commitment and sign the redline, we can be live in ~3–4 weeks with priority staffing.

Priyom Das
Staff Product Manager, Routing & Serving
Redwood Inference
